message.content: {"alternatives":[],"likely_cause":{"claim":"The most likely cause is that the edge-auth-b4 node has a significant clock skew due to failed NTP synchronization, causing it to reject tokens as not yet valid and resulting in high 401 error rates and session creation failures for users routed to this node.","evidence_ids":["log:1","log:2","log:4","log:7","log:9"]},"missing_evidence":[],"observations":[{"claim":"The edge-auth-b4 node failed NTP synchronization multiple times, with the last successful sync over 2 hours ago, leading to clock offset issues.","evidence_ids":["log:1","log:8"]},{"claim":"The edge-auth-b4 node rejected tokens with 'not_yet_valid' errors because the token's 'nbf' (not before) timestamp is about 4 minutes ahead of the local clock on the node.","evidence_ids":["log:2","log:4"]},{"claim":"The session-api service reports high 401 error rates (up to 91%) for requests routed to edge-auth-b4, while other edge-auth nodes have error rates below 2%.","evidence_ids":["log:3","log:9"]},{"claim":"Session creation failed for 1204 requests routed to edge-auth-b4 in the last 5 minutes, indicating a problem specific to this node affecting user sign-in.","evidence_ids":["log:7"]}],"outcome":"supported","suggested_checks":["Check the NTP synchronization status and configuration on the edge-auth-b4 node.","Verify the system clock and time zone settings on edge-auth-b4.","Review load balancing or routing rules to see why a subset of users are routed to edge-auth-b4.","Check token issuance times and validation logic for clock skew tolerance."]}
